goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
goldens.reasoning: C1 flags that should_block? changes stats while it is only checking an email. That is the same side-effect concern as G1.

goldens.comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate raises the regex domain-boundary bypass. C2 is about nil values, not the domain anchoring.

goldens.comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions the case-sensitive email lookup.

candidates: BlockedEmail.should_block? mutates state (match_count/last_match_at) and is called from email validation which can run multiple times per request (e.g., user.valid? then user.save), inflating stats and causing extra writes for a single signup attempt

email_in_restriction_setting? calls value =~ regexp which will raise if value is nil (e.g., missing email param) even though presence validation would already fail - need to guard validate_each / email_in_restriction_setting? against blank/nil values

pushObject(result.values.email) will add null/undefined if the server response omits values.email or returns it blank, leaving a non-string entry in rejectedEmails - should ensure value is present before caching

The computed property depends on rejectedEmails.@each but @each is mainly for observing per-item properties and can be unreliable for array membership changes with primitive items like strings - may not recompute when pushObject is called depending on Ember version
